title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: John x. 28–29 — the Father gave Christ certain sheep no force can snatch; giving = electing singular persons to defend and lead infallibly to eternal life
pass_a_gloss: The truth of the Major is plain from these testimonies of the Scriptures; Joann. x. 28, 29. No one snatches my sheep out of my hand. My Father, who gave them unto me, is greater than all: neither can anyone snatch them out of my Father's hand. I ask what is the sense of these words, The Father gave unto Christ certain sheep, which no force can snatch, except that God the Father by electing gave unto Christ certain singular persons, whom he decreed to defend against all the assaults and snares of the flesh, the world, and the devil, and at length infallibly to lead unto the fruition of everlasting life?
pass_b_english: The Major's truth is plain from these Scripture witnesses (John x. 28–29): No one snatches my sheep out of my hand. My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all; and no one can snatch them out of my Father's hand. What sense have the words The Father gave Christ certain sheep that no force can snatch — unless this: God the Father, by electing, gave Christ certain singular persons, whom he decreed to defend against all assaults and snares of flesh, world, and devil, and at last to lead infallibly to the fruition of everlasting life?
source_text: Majoris veritas ex hisce Scripturarum testimoniis patet; Joann. x. 28, 29. Nemo rapit oves meas de manu mea. Pater meus, qui eas dedit mihi, major omnibus est: neque quisquam potest eas rapere e manu Patris mei. Quaero quis sensus horum verborum, Pater Christo dedit oves certas, quas nulla vis potest rapere, nisi, Deus Pater eligendo dedit Christo singulares quasdam personas, quas decrevit contra omnes carnis, mundi, et diaboli impetus insidiasque defendere, atque tandem ad fruitionem aeternae vitae infallibiliter perducere?
